title: Weingart
description: A song credit set like a forme of hand-set metal type: three stepped lines of title, a process-red running time printed underneath, brass rule, a reversed slug, small text cascading down the right. Every line is a row of single sorts. Push one and it breaks into a staircase, each letter its own piece of lead one diagonal step below the letter before it, the step count following how far you drag; tracking between sorts never changes. The sorts are solid: a staircase that comes down onto the next line shoves exactly the letters it lands on, which breaks that line into its own staircase, and so on down the forme, each sort seating with its own knock, left to right, until the run locks against the edge of the chase. Only the red, printed in its own run, crosses the black, and where they overprint the two inks make a third, darker one.
intent: After Wolfgang Weingart's Basel letterpress experiments and his stepped Typografische Monatsblätter covers (1972–73): Swiss order broken from inside the system, using the real constraints of a press, quantised steps, letterspacing and overprinting, to make new rhythm. https://neugraphic.com/weingart/weingart-text2.html
